status: 18 substantial tasks covering construction of .expec from grammar and compiler foundations through connected projects, generation, evolution, additional outputs, and self-development. Detailed specifications and code design follow. Implementation has not started.

tasks.title: Define the .expec language grammar
tasks.hypothesis: A consistent, readable grammar can express the agreed software specifications precisely enough to implement and test.
tests: Express StoreGame with dependencies, public startup/saveGame capabilities, typed inputs and outputs, and behavior promises.
Express types, interfaces, components, functions, local types, and generic fields such as Pair<Number>.
Express literal results, prose expectations, scenarios, and ordered communications.
Express declarations and examples inline or in referenced files; identify malformed and ambiguous syntax.
tasks.learnings: Grammar candidate ready; relationships derive from declared dependencies, construction/capability signatures, outputs, and fields. No dedicated relationship keyword is required. Retain shortening as design learning.

tasks.title: Build the compiler and validation
tasks.hypothesis: A runnable compiler can turn valid source into a shared specification model and reject invalid contracts with useful diagnostics.
tests: Set up and run the compiler and its independent acceptance tests from a clean checkout.
Compile StoreGame and supplied dependencies; preserve typed contracts, examples, ordered messages, and source locations.
Reject unavailable names, the saveGame/save mismatch, incompatible types, and invalid contract or scenario flow.
Keep unfinished behavior visible; unsupported composition and an incorrect compiler cannot masquerade as success.
tasks.learnings: Specified compile/read/validate contracts and acceptance cases. Relationships derive from declared uses; implementation work is beginning.

tasks.title: Implement configuration and dependency management
tasks.hypothesis: One manifest can maintain project settings, output choices, versions, and the dependencies required to build the specified software.
tests: Configure StoreGame's project path, TypeScript output, version, and build settings.
Declare specification libraries separately from target packages such as Vite and Supabase.
Resolve compatible declared dependencies and expose missing or conflicting requirements.
Change a configured destination or output; the next operation uses the new settings.

tasks.title: Implement imports and specification composition
tasks.hypothesis: Authors can split and reuse specifications without changing their meaning or making undeclared names available.
tests: Import PlayerStateSnapshot and ShoppingCart from declared sources; their references resolve.
Keep StoreGame examples inline or in a separate file and obtain equivalent specifications.
Enforce local-type visibility and report missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or invalid cyclic references.
A nearby unimported file does not silently supply a missing declaration.

tasks.title: Implement project connection and initialization
tasks.hypothesis: An author can connect the intended software project or choose to initialize one before output is written.
tests: Connect an existing project through the manifest and use its actual source files.
With no project connected, ask whether to initialize one and honor the selected destination and target.
Declining initialization creates nothing; an invalid connection is reported.
Initialize the selected target's project structure and required dependency setup.

tasks.title: Implement the extensible output API
tasks.hypothesis: Interchangeable outputs can use the same resolved specification through the agreed operations and configured project context.
tests: Construct an output with target options and a live project-context component.
Exercise create(spec), insert(specDiff), update(specDiff), read(id), search(id), and delete(id) using SpecIdentifier.
Select a supported output from the manifest without changing the parser.
Add a sample output and report unsupported operations or mappings explicitly.

tasks.title: Implement live project reading and searching
tasks.hypothesis: The tool can inspect the complete current representation of a concept and its actual relationships, including handwritten and unspecified code.
tests: Read StoreGame across files, including public methods, private fields, helpers, and handwritten bodies.
Search its definition, outgoing dependencies, and all resolvable incoming uses, including an unspecified consumer.
Edit project code between calls; the next read or search reflects the edit.
Inspection changes no files and discloses unsupported or unresolved code instead of claiming complete coverage.

tasks.title: Implement specification identity and change comparison
tasks.hypothesis: Stable associations and live comparisons can identify intended changes without guessing which existing code belongs to a specification.
tests: Associate StoreGame and its members with an existing single-file or distributed implementation.
Compare specification versions and identify additions, updates, moves, renames, and removals.
Expected dependencies a,b,c versus actual a,b,d reports missing c and extra d.
Ambiguous correspondence remains unresolved; a similar name does not silently establish identity.

tasks.title: Generate TypeScript contracts and implementation scaffolds
tasks.hypothesis: Declared concepts can become useful TypeScript structure while unfinished behavior stays explicit.
tests: Generate StoreGame's public signatures and the SystemConfig, PlayerStateSnapshot, ShoppingCart, and Pair types.
Map appropriate concepts to classes, interfaces, types, or functions without forcing every concept into a class.
A new capability has an explicit not-implemented body; a prose promise does not invent its implementation.
Render required target dependencies and report unsupported mappings.

tasks.title: Generate readable executable specifications and domain helpers
tasks.hypothesis: Specified examples can become readable tests with reusable domain helpers and meaningful checks.
tests: Generate a shopper test using bookIsAvailable, startWithEmptyBasket, addBook, and expectBookQuantity.
Turn explicit inputs, observations, and literal expectations into real comparisons; wrong results fail.
Generate typed helper contracts and reuse declared operations across scenarios.
A prose expectation without an executable observation remains a visible unfinished obligation.

tasks.title: Implement scenario setup and execution integration
tasks.hypothesis: Readable generated tests can exercise real software through reusable setup and drivers without hiding implementation details in the scenarios.
tests: Share declared fixture setup and pass action results to later observations.
Run scenarios independently without leaked state.
Connect the same domain operation to a real application driver and inspect the system's actual result.
An unavailable driver or failed observation cannot count as a passing scenario.

tasks.title: Implement project updates that preserve handwritten code
tasks.hypothesis: Specification changes can alter connected source structure while retaining implementation work and exposing conflicts.
tests: Create files or insert capabilities; existing bodies, private state, helpers, and unrelated files survive.
Update signatures or expectations, and apply established renames or moves in single-file and distributed projects.
Remove obsolete generated structure while retaining handwritten work and reporting affected consumers.
A conflicting manual edit is reported instead of silently overwritten; changed behavior may still require implementation.

tasks.title: Assemble repeatable builds into connected projects
tasks.hypothesis: A build can coordinate validation, selected outputs, and project updates with clear results across specification versions.
tests: Build a valid StoreGame specification into the manifest-connected project with its selected outputs.
An invalid specification leaves the project's files unchanged.
Repeat an unchanged build without duplicate artifacts or further edits.
Increment the manifest version, apply the specification diff, and report changes and remaining implementation obligations.

tasks.title: Implement UML structure and interaction outputs
tasks.hypothesis: The shared specification can communicate both structural relationships and explicitly described interactions through UML.
tests: Show StoreGame, its contracts, types, and declared dependency relationships.
Show a save interaction in the specified participant and message order.
A dependency alone does not invent a message sequence; missing interaction detail is reported.
Changing the specification updates the corresponding diagram consistently.

tasks.title: Implement Markdown documentation output
tasks.hypothesis: Readable project documentation can stay consistent with the same contracts and examples used for code and tests.
tests: Export StoreGame's capabilities, inputs, outputs, dependencies, relationships, and examples.
Distinguish executable checks from unfinished prose expectations.
Update generated documentation while preserving handwritten additions.
Use the configured output API and destination.

tasks.title: Implement Kotlin, Java, and Python targets
tasks.hypothesis: Additional code targets can preserve the same specification meaning through their own code, test, inspection, and update support.
tests: Generate equivalent contracts and supported acceptance examples in Kotlin, Java, and Python.
Read and search each target's existing project representation, disclosing discovery limitations.
Apply supported changes without losing handwritten implementations.
Report unsupported mappings and dynamic references rather than guessing equivalent behavior.

tasks.title: Develop .expec through its own specifications and a real pilot
tasks.hypothesis: Using .expec on itself and StoreGame can test the proposed workflow and reveal requirements the implementation misses.
tests: Describe compiler contracts and acceptance examples in .expec, then generate and evolve supported parts of the compiler project.
Check the generated tool independently and retain a usable bootstrap path.
Evolve StoreGame from local persistence to Supabase while retaining implementation work and exposing changed obligations.
Record actual results and revise tasks, stories, and the pitch when the examples or approach need to change.

tasks.title: Package the tool and support exporter development
tasks.hypothesis: Authors and output developers can install and use .expec without relying on repository internals.
tests: Install a versioned package and follow a project initialization, validation, build, and revision walkthrough.
Implement and register an additional output through the documented API.
Run shared output-contract checks, including read/search responsibilities and unsupported-feature reporting.
Document supported targets, dependency setup, common diagnostics, and remaining limitations.
